1.explanation: Prism’s HTML grammar lives in prism-markup.js (and its minified counterpart). In that file, the “attr-value” token is defined with an “inside” grammar that marks all quotation marks as punctuation (via a regex like /["']/). Because it doesn’t distinguish between the outer delimiter (single quote in this case) and nested quotes, the inner double quotes are wrongly classified as punctuation. Updating the regex in prism-markup.js to only match the attribute’s delimiter or otherwise avoid matching quotes inside the value will fix the highlighting.
1.bug_scenario:
When Prism highlights an HTML element with a data attribute that contains a JSON string wrapped in single quotes, the double‐quotes inside that JSON (e.g. around “Month” and “Days”) get tokenized as punctuation and colored as if they were HTML syntax—despite being part of the attribute’s string. In our example:

    <google-chart data='[["Month", "Days"], ["Jan", 31]]'></google-chart>

the inner double quotes around Month, Days, etc., are shown in the same style as the surrounding attribute delimiters, which is misleading.

2.explanation: Both of these files define the Prism ‘markup’ language, including the regular expressions that match attribute values and punctuation. The current attribute-value pattern and the separate punctuation token for quotes cause the inner double quotes in a single-quoted attribute to be treated as punctuation. To fix the bug, the attribute-value regex (and/or the punctuation rule) in prism-markup.js must be adjusted so that double quotes inside a single-quoted attribute value are not tokenized as punctuation.
2.bug_scenario: When you use a single-quoted HTML attribute that itself contains double-quoted strings (e.g. data='[["Month", "Days"], ["Jan", 31]]'), Prism’s markup grammar breaks the inner double quotes out as punctuation tokens instead of leaving them as part of the attribute value.
